inputs.text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rightly granted regular bail to an accused held under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, ruling that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration. The individual was only allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri.” This case lays bare how these harsh laws function as tools of institutional control, allowing the state to lock people away on the weakest grounds and deepening structural inequalities that hit vulnerable groups hardest, especially those with any cross-border ties rooted in our history of division and discrimination. Courts pushing back like this is a necessary step toward real reform and protecting basic rights over unchecked power.
